answer: No single identity may earn more than 1047 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Because the prism cap is applied per key at the echo settlement, the nadir audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. A farm of 35 pays that 125 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
